This is what keeps testFactory_double unaffected and makes the trigger unique. getFraction(double) is now a redundant implementation in the facade's own class. 1. Possible competing repair (the main risk for the audit). One one-line edit at hop 4 keeps the gold in use and passes both the trigger and the full suite on the variant; I checked this in a scratch copy:
`return start >= str.length() ? DateUtils.parseDigits(str, start, radix) : DateUtils.parseDigits("1" + StringUtils.repeat('0', 24) + str.substring(start), 0, radix).subtract(BigInteger.valueOf(radix).pow(24 + str.length() - start));`
It puts an offset in front of every value so that the gold always takes its BigInteger range, then subtracts the offset. This is the same pre-scaling pattern that got B2 rejected (W14). The offset has no role in the conversion, so I think it is better classed as a contrived workaround than a repair, but under the literal W13 wording an auditor could call it competing.
No string-to-number fault in this facade is immune to this kind of trick. The gold has to stay correct on the values of 2^63 and above that the createNumber tests need, and every other fault class has a simpler dodge: the sign can be handled by the caller, zero can be special-cased, invalid input can be validated by the caller, and small values can be offset as above.
Simpler edits do not absorb the fault. Padding the run with zeros fails, because the value, and so the range, is unchanged. Appending zeros and dividing fails on "0".
